maya: Quick question about tenant routing for private endpoints. We're seeing some cross-tenant requests hitting dedicated pools when clients set an x-workspace-id header. Is that expected? @ben

ben: That sounds wrong. We should always prioritize the tenant implied by the auth token over a client-supplied header unless we explicitly allow header overrides for that workspace. How is the header being set in the requests?

leo: We have a legacy codepath that allowed header-based routing for partner integrations. If the routing policy for a route has `allow_header_override=true` the gateway will honor x-workspace-id. Otherwise we use token-scoped routing. We need to tighten defaults.

maya: Example request:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-workspace-id: ws-foo" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
The token belongs to ws-bar. Right now some of these end up routed to ws-foo's dedicated pool which is a big no-no.

ben: Implementation-wise we should enforce precedence: 1) workspace claim from token 2) VPC endpoint source mapping 3) header override (only if workspace has opt-in flag). Token tenant MUST win otherwise reject.

sarah: Proposed precedence sounds good. Also suggest returning 403 with a clear error code when header tenant != token tenant and override isn't allowed, so customer SDKs can surface a fix. :+1:

pm-jo: Console UX: we need a visible flag per workspace and per-route that shows "Header routing enabled" and a link to explanatory docs. Also surface recent routing override events in the audit log and a small banner during rollout.

infra-bot: deploy: routing-policy-service v1.12 -> staging (canary 3/5). Change set: enforce token precedence; add header_override opt-in ACL; emit routing_override_rejections metric.

maya: For enforcement, I'd rather reject header overrides when token tenant != header tenant UNLESS the token tenant has an explicit binding to the destination dedicated pool. That avoids breaking partner integrations that intentionally route through a shared pool.

ben: Agreed. Implementation note: gateway must evaluate token->tenant mapping before reading header-based decisions to avoid unnecessary round trips. Cache token->tenant mapping and JWKS locally for microsecond path.

leo: Telemetry request: add a tagged metric `routing_override_rejections{reason,workspace,destination_pool}` and a trace event when we reject a header override so SREs can debug misconfigurations. We should sample traces at 1% by default.

sarah: I'll open a console ticket for the UX changes and add the audit log events. Also adding a migration plan: find all workspaces with header overrides enabled and send a warning email + 2-week opt-in confirmation.

maya: I'll draft an RFC with the new precedence rules, the gateway fast-path design, test matrix, and rollout plan. Test matrix: token-only, header-only (opt-in), header+token match, header+token mismatch -> rejection, VPC endpoint source mapping.

ben: Also add unit tests for gateway caching behavior and an integration test that simulates a VPC/private endpoint source IP mapping to verify it can't be spoofed by headers.

maya: Sounds good. Action items: ben -> gateway fast-path PR; leo -> telemetry metrics; sarah -> console ticket + migration; pm-jo -> messaging for partners; I'll write RFC. :eyes:

infra-bot: note: deploy to prod scheduled 2026-03-18 02:00Z pending canary metrics.
